# AudioPhysx — audio that reacts to the world

> A MetaSound and Blueprint toolkit for responsive, carefully designed Unreal Engine audio. AudioPhysx brings together flexible sample players, physically

- [AudioPhysx — audio that reacts to the world](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/readme.md): AudioPhysx — audio that reacts to the world
- [Getting started with AudioPhysx](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/getting-started/readme.md): The fastest way to understand AudioPhysx is to make one sound work end to end before building a complicated acoustic system. You can begin with an ordinary imported recording, one trigger and a stereo MetaSound Source.
- [The AudioPhysx MetaSound library](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/metasound/readme.md): The current native source contains 24 nodes. They are divided by the job they perform rather than the feature that first inspired them: ten Wave Players
- [Bringing game-world information into audio](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/blueprint/readme.md): MetaSound processes audio and audio-rate events, but it does not automatically know where a projectile travelled, what wall is between a source and listener, or which Physical Material was returned by a collision query.
- [Learn by building something audible](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/examples/readme.md): Node reference pages explain individual tools; the examples show how several parts fit together in an actual listening task. They deliberately begin with ordinary Wave Assets and small MetaSound graphs rather than a large demonstration project that needs dozens of dependencies.
- [Support and compatibility](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/support/readme.md): AudioPhysx adds native audio players, world-query integrations and DSP nodes to Unreal Engine, so troubleshooting is easiest when you separate build and registration, event and asset playback, and world-derived control data.

## Getting started

- [Requirements and terminology](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/getting-started/requirements.md): AudioPhysx is a native C++ plugin for Unreal Engine. The code reviewed for this edition targets UE 5.8.4 and includes the stereo conversion and RPM playback system.
- [Installing the plugin](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/getting-started/installation.md): AudioPhysx can be installed either as a finished, compatible Fab code plugin or from a complete source distribution. This guide describes both approaches, but the current documentation package does not contain or redistribute the paid plugin source.
- [Your first AudioPhysx MetaSound](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/getting-started/first-metasound.md): This example builds an action sound with three stages: a short click, a mechanical movement and a final latch. You will trigger the entire action once, and the Sequence Wave Player will start each recording after the preceding one finishes.
- [Stereo routing and deliberate mono conversion](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/getting-started/stereo-routing.md): AudioPhysx's current design is stereo throughout audio-bearing playback and processing, with a dedicated node for conversion to mono. This is useful because it avoids discarding information before the sound designer has decided whether that information matters.
- [Triggers, audio buffers and completion](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/getting-started/signals-and-completion.md): A MetaSound graph contains different kinds of wires because it describes both events and continuous sound. Play, Stop, Reset and On Finished are triggers that represent moments.
- [A practical setup checklist](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/getting-started/checklist.md): Most silent or incorrect AudioPhysx graphs can be diagnosed by working from the simplest part of the chain outward. First make sure a known-good Wave Asset plays through a basic stereo Source with the correct Out Left and Out Right wiring.

## MetaSound nodes

- [Playback: what should play, and when?](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/metasound/playback.md): A convincing sound library needs more than a folder of recordings. It needs a clear decision about when an event begins, whether recordings overlap, how a variation is chosen, and when the audible result should actually end.
- [Acoustics: why does a place change the sound?](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/metasound/acoustics.md): A recording played through a loudspeaker should not sound identical in every physical situation. It may be blocked by a door, travel around an opening, lose high-frequency detail when the source faces away, or produce an initial set of room reflections.
- [Propagation: when sound takes time to reach us](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/metasound/propagation.md): Propagation concerns how a sound changes while travelling from its source to the listener. In the real world, an explosion heard at a great distance arrives after its flash, and a moving source can exhibit Doppler shift.
- [QoL: fewer repeated control graphs](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/metasound/qol.md): Not everything in AudioPhysx needs to process audio samples. Many MetaSounds become difficult to maintain because the same housekeeping logic is rebuilt
- [Interfaces and external audio parameters](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/metasound/interfaces.md): AudioPhysx separates gameplay-side world queries from audio rendering. One consequence is that some MetaSound inputs are fed by named parameters or registered interfaces rather than being authored independently in each graph.

## Blueprint integration

- [Projectile flybys from a path segment](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/blueprint/flyby.md): A useful projectile near-miss sound should represent a projectile that actually passed near the listener, not every time any weapon fired. AudioPhysx's flyby helper accepts the start and end of a projectile path segment, its speed, and an audible radius.
- [Querying sound routes through the level](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/blueprint/acoustic-paths.md): A line from source to listener may be clear, obstructed by a wall or partly bypassed through an opening. AudioPhysx provides a game-thread acoustic path solver to estimate how these possibilities affect the sound.
- [Playing sounds from Blueprint](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/blueprint/playback-helpers.md): Many AudioPhysx sounds begin in ordinary gameplay code. A character performs an interaction, a projectile hits a surface, or a persistent emitter needs to follow an Actor.
- [Representing the acoustic scene](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/blueprint/components.md): AudioPhysx includes optional components that associate sounds, physical obstacles and openings with real level objects. They are designed to let a managed acoustic system reason about where a sound begins and what it passes through.
- [Acoustic materials, thickness and performance settings](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/blueprint/materials-and-settings.md): An Acoustic Physical Material describes the model you want AudioPhysx to use for a surface's sound-transmission behaviour. The current

## Examples and recipes

- [Randomized one-shots](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/examples/randomized-one-shot.md): Primary AudioPhysx tools: AP: Random Wave Player
- [Automatic weapon with RPM](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/examples/automatic-weapon.md): Primary AudioPhysx tools: AP: Start Loop End Player
- [Multi-stage variation](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/examples/random-sequence.md): Primary AudioPhysx tools: AP: Random Sequence Wave Player
- [Material-dependent footsteps](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/examples/material-footsteps.md): Primary AudioPhysx tools: AP: Surface or PhysMat Wave Player
- [Projectile near-miss audio](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/examples/projectile-flyby.md): Primary AudioPhysx tools: AP: Flyby Wave Player + Blueprint helper
- [Sound behind a wall](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/examples/acoustic-obstruction.md): Primary AudioPhysx tools: AP: Material Transmission or Acoustic Paths

## Support & release notes

- [Troubleshooting AudioPhysx](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/support/troubleshooting.md): When an effect does not behave as expected, debug from the outside in. First verify Unreal can play the chosen recording. Then verify the MetaSound receives its starting trigger.
- [Frequently asked questions](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/support/faq.md): Why make all the audio nodes stereo? The previous mono-first design forced information out of a stereo recording before a sound designer had decided whether that information was useful.
- [Compatibility and technical boundaries](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/support/compatibility.md): These pages are based on the AudioPhysx UE 5.8.4 source package uploaded for this documentation revision. They describe what is present in the code and how it is intended to be used.
- [Development and documentation history](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/support/changelog.md): Stereo documentation revision — 27 November 2026. The site now describes 24 current native MetaSound nodes, including the new AP: Stereo to Mono converter. References use the updated In Left, In Right, Out Left and Out Right audio paths where present.
